news.title: Iran War Doubles Egypt’s LNG Bill as Gas Output Keeps Falling
news.summary: The war on Iran has doubled what Egypt pays for imported LNG, and Cairo is deferring cargoes into 2027 and burning fuel oil in its power plants to hold down the bill. Egypt’s own output fell to 3.63 bcf/d in August as older fields declined faster than new wells came online, and the petroleum ministry has now extended the deadline for bids on 14 exploration blocks meant to reverse that decline to December 14 after companies asked for more time. analysis.summary: The Iran war and falling domestic gas output have doubled Egypt's LNG import costs, forcing Cairo to defer LNG cargoes and burn fuel oil in power plants.
analysis.rationale: Switching utility power generation from natural gas to fuel oil increases oil product demand, while ongoing Middle East conflict and LNG force majeure highlight regional energy supply strains.

news.title: Global Diesel Crunch Set to Last Well Into 2027
news.summary: While crude oil imports in Asia have reached pre-war levels, imports of refined products remain weak as gasoline and diesel imports from the Middle East have crashed amid reduced refining capacity. Asia’s oil import story these days is a reflection of the global oil markets—crude oil availability has significantly increased since the early summer lows and flows out of the Middle East have largely recovered, but supply of gasoline, and especially diesel, has sharply dropped since the Iran war began at the end of February. Reduced refinery…

analysis.summary: Asian crude imports and Middle East crude flows have largely recovered to pre-war levels, while refined product supply faces a severe crunch lasting into 2027 due to reduced refining capacity.
analysis.rationale: Recovered crude availability and flows exert downward price pressure, whereas acute, prolonged refining bottlenecks and diesel shortages create upward pressure across the petroleum complex.

news.title: US Crude Oil Inventories Still in Freefall
news.summary: The American Petroleum Institute (API) estimated that crude oil inventories in the United States fell by 5.267 million barrels in the week ending October 30. In the week prior, US crude oil inventories fell by a staggering 2.031 million barrels. Commercial crude oil inventories excluding the SPR have lost more than 64 million barrels over the last 29 weeks, and 12 million over this year, according to API data, which has been kept in check in part thanks to draws from the SPR. For the week ending October 30, 400,000 barrels of crude oil left the…

analysis.summary: API estimated a large 5.267-million-barrel drop in US crude inventories for the week ending October 30, extending a multi-month commercial inventory draw.
analysis.rationale: A substantial weekly inventory draw of more than 5 million barrels signals physical market tightening and robust demand, applying clear upward pressure on crude prices.

news.title: Iran War Triples Logistics Costs for Oil Services Firms
news.summary: Oilfield services companies are paying as much as three times their usual logistics costs in the Middle East, with fuel expenses doubling and labor costs climbing by as much as 40%, as the Iran war continues to disrupt equipment deliveries and project operations. Executives speaking Tuesday at the ADIPEC energy conference in Abu Dhabi described mounting financial pressure from the nine-month conflict, which has damaged infrastructure, forced employee evacuations, and made moving equipment through the Strait of Hormuz increasingly difficult. analysis.summary: Oilfield services firms report tripled logistics costs, doubled fuel expenses, and significant operational disruption in the Middle East due to the ongoing Iran war.
analysis.rationale: Infrastructure damage, employee evacuations, and transit impediments in the Strait of Hormuz jeopardize upstream support operations and elevate regional supply-disruption risk premiums.
